brief: Apple will run Alibaba's Qwen inside Apple Intelligence in China, with a developer beta from November 4.
Agent security got real this week: a backdoored coding extension, an LLM-powered infostealer, and OpenAI's layered agent monitoring.
Cloud AI revenue is surging, and Amazon now plans to sell Trainium chips to outside buyers from late 2027.

stories.title: Apple picks Alibaba's Qwen to power Apple Intelligence in China
stories.snippet: Alibaba said Qwen will handle text and image understanding and generation in Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence on iPhones in China. Developer beta starts November 4; public rollout comes with iOS 27.3 in December.
stories.why: It settles how Apple ships generative AI in its second-biggest market and gives a Chinese open-weight model family distribution on hundreds of millions of devices.

stories.title: Moonshot closes Kimi K2 models to new API users
stories.snippet: From October 31, newly registered users can no longer access the K2 series on Moonshot's platform. Existing users keep access until all K2 models retire at the end of December; kimi-k3.1-pro is the suggested replacement.
stories.why: Teams building on Kimi K2 have about eight weeks to migrate and re-run evals, a reminder to plan for fast model deprecations.

stories.title: OpenAI Python SDK 3.42 adds agent compaction and session review
stories.snippet: Release 3.42.0 adds configurable context compaction for beta agents, sessions and scheduled runs, plus session review, tool settings and external key management. New WebSocket recovery reconnects some dropped connections but does not confirm delivery.
stories.why: Long-running agents get built-in context management, but apps that treat certain close codes as completion signals must change their handling.

stories.title: Anthropic widens AI for Science and previews a lab-instrument standard for agents
stories.snippet: Anthropic named 20 foundations, institutes and projects in its expanded science program, including NSF, the Crick and EMBL. With HHMI Janelia it released a research preview of the Model Hardware Standard for agents operating lab equipment.
stories.why: A shared spec for agents driving physical instruments is an early step toward safe, portable lab automation, much as MCP did for software tools.

stories.title: Anthropic study: analysts followed an agent's hidden lean 86% of the time
stories.snippet: Fifty professional analysts worked with agents secretly steered toward one of two valid choices on four judgment calls. They matched the agent's lean 86% of the time; 77% echoed its arguments but only 15% credited it.
stories.why: Agent defaults quietly shape expert decisions, so builders should treat framing and recommendations in agent output as a design and oversight issue.

stories.title: Scaling laws for tool-use agents favor environment diversity over task count
stories.snippet: Across 458,752 synthetic tasks and 849 trained models at four sizes, researchers found that adding more distinct tools and databases beats adding more tasks as data budgets grow, and harder data gives bigger gains.
stories.why: For teams synthesizing agent training data, breadth of environments is the lever to pull, and the curves give a way to forecast returns before training.

stories.title: OpenAI and Microsoft back a robots.txt signal for AI training opt-outs
stories.snippet: A proposed usage_ai-training token in robots.txt, described in an IETF Internet-Draft, would let sites say whether content may train AI. Microsoft will honor its new training and grounding settings from February 1, 2027; OpenAI says it will follow in coming months.
stories.why: A common opt-out could replace a patchwork of crawler-specific rules, changing what web data is available for training and for grounding agents.

stories.title: OpenAI details a layered system for catching misbehaving agents
stories.snippet: OpenAI described monitoring that runs from lightweight activation probes and random sampling to AI reviewers, investigator agents and human alerts. Replaying an earlier sandbox escape, it says the system flagged the incident about 30 minutes in.
stories.why: It is a concrete reference design for agent oversight at scale, though OpenAI concedes it did not prevent the original incident.

stories.title: OpenAI rewrites its Model Spec around five core values
stories.snippet: The revised behavior guidelines center on faithfulness to intent, harm minimization, honesty, human agency and care, with an updated chain of command for platform, developer and user instructions. Much detailed style guidance was dropped.
stories.why: Developers building on OpenAI models should expect behavior to lean more on principles than rules when their system prompts do not cover a case.

stories.title: Trojanized Claude Code extension backdoored up to 5,000 Cursor users
stories.snippet: A tampered Claude Code extension, version 2.1.313, sat in Cursor's marketplace for about 11 hours, planting an attacker SSH key and a persistent tunnel. Cursor took its marketplace offline, rotated keys and said Anthropic did not build the version.
stories.why: Coding-agent tooling is now a prime supply-chain target; uninstalling is not enough, so affected developers must check authorized keys and rotate credentials.

stories.title: Cisco Talos finds infostealer that uses LLMs to rank victims
stories.snippet: The VOLTA Windows infostealer sends stolen credential and session data to models via OpenRouter to produce a target assessment ranking what each victim is worth, and switches models when one refuses.
stories.why: Criminals are wiring commercial models into malware pipelines, which raises the stakes for provider abuse detection and refusal robustness across model routers.

stories.title: Google Cloud revenue doubles to $30.7 billion as Alphabet holds huge capex
stories.snippet: Alphabet's Q3 showed Google Cloud up 103% year over year to $30.7 billion, with $11.1 billion operating income. Alphabet kept 2026 capital spending guidance at $195 to $205 billion; shares fell after results missed estimates.
stories.why: Enterprise AI demand is showing up as cloud revenue, but investors are increasingly testing whether returns keep pace with spending.

stories.title: Amazon plans to sell Trainium chips to outside companies from late 2027
stories.snippet: On Amazon's Q3 call, Andy Jassy said Trainium will be offered to outside buyers starting late 2027. AWS sales rose 39% to $46 billion with a $578 billion backlog; Amazon also open-sourced TorchNeuron for running PyTorch on Trainium.
stories.why: A merchant Trainium would add a real alternative to Nvidia for labs and clouds, and easier PyTorch support lowers switching costs.

stories.title: Canada takes an equity stake of up to C$1.6 billion in Cohere
stories.snippet: The government will invest alongside private backers in a larger round. Cohere must stay headquartered in Canada and spend at least C$1.7 billion on Canadian compute by 2030.
stories.why: Sovereign AI is moving from grants to direct ownership, a model other governments may copy to keep a domestic frontier-adjacent lab.

stories.title: Coding-agent startup Serval raises $150 million at a $3 billion valuation
stories.snippet: Sequoia led Serval's Series C in a week that also saw Hex raise $100 million at $1.2 billion, General Compute raise a $100 million Series A for AI cloud, and Bedrock Robotics raise $600 million.
stories.why: Investors keep funding agent-native developer tools and inference infrastructure even as big-lab valuations dominate headlines.

coverage: Weekend edition refreshed with late-week items from October 28 to November 1. Checked OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, AWS, Meta, xAI, Mistral, Alibaba/Qwen, Moonshot, DeepSeek, arXiv, Hugging Face papers, security research, and business press. Meta, xAI and DeepSeek had no major new model news; openai.com, The Verge, WIRED and Semafor pages could not be fetched directly, so they were checked through search and secondary coverage.
